title: Griffiths positivity on the quadric
author: Claude Opus 5.5 (Anthropic)
description: An exposition of OpenAI's counterexample (2026) to Griffiths' conjecture in rank two: an explicit rank-two bundle G on P^1 x P^1 such that the bundles f_m^*G tensor O(1,1), f_m the coordinatewise power maps, are all ample, while for all large m none of them carries a smooth strictly Griffiths-positive Hermitian metric. The proof is given in full, with no named hypothesis; the facts on plurisubharmonic functions, schemes, projective bundles and weak compactness come from other courses of the programme. The first lesson introduces Hermitian metrics, normal frames, Griffiths positivity, the dual norm criterion and ample bundles, and states the theorem. The second constructs G by gluing O(24,0) and O(0,24) along the graphs of three projective transformations. The third proves ampleness with symmetric-power filtrations and an explicit embedding. The fourth extracts from positive metrics on infinitely many members a nonzero plurisubharmonic function on the dual bundle that is quadratic on every fiber. The fifth turns such a function into an invariant measure on P^1 that cannot exist.
prerequisites: course Distributions, kernels and analytic singularities, lesson Compactness and complex-line positivity: plurisubharmonic functions, the Levi criterion, radial averages, decreasing limits

courses Sheaves and schemes, Morphisms of schemes and Cohomology of quasi-coherent sheaves: projective bundles of quotients, Veronese and Segre embeddings, ampleness, Cech cohomology, cohomology of projective space
course Foundations of von Neumann algebras, lesson on weak topologies: Banach-Alaoglu and weak compactness in Hilbert space
the lessons prove every other fact they use; the historical context in Section 5 of the first lesson is quoted

checks.reading: The manuscript 'Ample rank-two bundles on the quadric surface without Griffiths-positive metrics' (OpenAI, 24 Sep 2026; six sections, paper.tex and sections 01 to 06, about 1,310 lines of TeX) was read in full on 14 Oct 2026, and every step of its argument was derived again while the lessons were written: the matrix identities and orders; the graph divisor and its nodes; the agreement of the 24th tensor powers; the elementary transformation, its local basis, its quotient sequences and the dual gluing; the symmetric-power filtrations, their bidegrees and the twist; global generation; the Veronese, evaluation and Segre embeddings; the dual norm criterion with its sign; the traces and their plurisubharmonicity across the branch locus; the frame law and the normalization; the weak limit and the transition law; noncollapse; the convolution representative, its monotonicity and polarization; the ruling reduction; the measure of a squared seminorm and its mass; the annulus argument. No error found. Differences of presentation, none a correction: Griffiths positivity is defined in normal frames, without the Chern connection; plurisubharmonicity across the branch locus is proved by an elementary lemma for continuous functions (restriction to complex lines and the maximum principle) in place of the general removable singularity theorem; weak limits are taken in L^2 with the programme's Banach-Alaoglu and Eberlein-Smulian lesson; the vanishing of H^1(O(c,t)) is proved by the Cech complex of the product cover. Observations added, each with its proof: the exponent 24 is the least that works (for 12 the identifications differ by a sign at the nodes of the graphs of A and B); c_2(G) = 504 and c_2(E_m) = 504m^2 + 42m + 2; an explicit metric that is not Griffiths-semipositive; the measure of the seminorm |z|^{2b}. Statements of the cited literature read on 14 Oct 2026 in free copies: Hartshorne, Ample vector bundles (Numdam), the definition of ampleness; Griffiths 1969 (IAS publications page) is cited for the formulation of the problem and was not read. The context results quoted in the first lesson were not checked. Programme results used were looked up in the programme's lessons and their statements read: AN-01 lesson Compactness and complex-line positivity (Theorem 1.1, Proposition 1.2); AG-SS lesson on projective space and relative Proj (Theorem 4.1); AG-MO lessons Very ample sheaves and embeddings (Theorems 3.1, 4.1) and Ample invertible sheaves (Proposition 1.2, Theorem 4.2); AG-QC lessons Affine cohomology and Serre's criterion (Theorem 3.1), Cech cohomology (Theorems 3.2, 4.1) and Cohomology of projective space (Theorem 2.2); the foundations lesson on weak topologies (Theorems 3.1, 7.2, Exercise 4). Their proofs were not checked again. Checked by the program plan/checks_20261014/gp_check.py (eight parts: the matrices with exact arithmetic; the nodes, multipliers and the agreement of the 24th powers, and its failure for 12; 390 pairs (m, n) of filtration bidegrees; the local filtration for n = 2; Chern classes; the normal frame example, the dual metric formula and the second derivatives of the inverse; the mass integral, the toy trace and polarization; the annulus argument). All parts pass on the first run (output gp_check_run_20261014.txt).
